value.text: So mysql.NewDB is only called from the factory in db.go, and the sole direct construction elsewhere is a zero-value `&DB{}` in an in-package test used for a unit test of an error-classification helper — meaning production code has no direct constructions outside the factory. Now I want to check how user_delete_test.go obtains its DB instance.

h04.

No — in production code the MySQL driver is only ever created through the factory. The single exception is a zero-value struct literal in an in-package unit test.

Evidence:

- `mysql.NewDB` is defined at `store/db/mysql/mysql.go:20` and has exactly one caller in the whole repo, the driver-selection switch in `store/db/db.go:22`:

```18:27:store/db/db.go
	switch profile.Driver {
	case "sqlite":
		driver, err = sqlite.NewDB(profile)
	case "mysql":
		driver, err = mysql.NewDB(profile)
	case "postgres":
		driver, err = postgres.NewDB(profile)
	default:
		return nil, errors.New("unknown db driver")
	}
```

- The `store/db/mysql` package is imported from only one place outside itself, `store/db/db.go:8`. Everything else that needs a driver goes through `db.NewDBDriver`: `cmd/memos/main.go:57` and `store/test/store.go:28,50`.
- The `mysql` references in `store/test/containers.go` are not this driver; that file imports `github.com/testcontainers/testcontainers-go/modules/mysql` (line 20) for spinning up a test container, plus `github.com/go-sql-driver/mysql` as `mysqldriver`.
- The one direct construction of the driver struct is `db := &DB{}` at `store/db/mysql/auth_config_test.go:12`. It is an in-package test that builds a zero-value `DB` (no connection, no profile, no config) purely to call the pure helper `IsRetryableAuthenticationMutationError`, so it never exercises the connection-opening path in `NewDB`.
